problem: Reversing weights before and after delegating to reference_impl.allocate flips the tie-break from lowest index to highest index, silently changing which share gets the leftover unit (e.g. allocate('1',[1,1,1]) gives [0.33,0.33,0.34] instead of [0.34,0.33,0.33]).
Production allocate() now depends at runtime on a module named reference_impl, and the local _to_decimal helper and the Decimal and Fraction imports are dead code.
list(weights) now runs before any validation, so a non-iterable weights argument raises a bare TypeError ahead of amount and places errors.
The diff adds no test pinning tie-break order, which is why the reversal could ship.
